question: Explain object-oriented design and the SOLID principles. Show me with an example.

scenes.sub: Design code so new features are added, not edited in.
scenes.say: Object oriented design and SOLID. Five letters that sound abstract. We will make them concrete with one small refactoring.

scenes.head: Analogy: a wall socket
scenes.say: Think of a wall socket. A lamp plugs in. A laptop plugs in. Tomorrow you buy a kettle, and it plugs in too. Nobody rewires the wall. The socket is an interface, and anything that fits it works. Good object oriented design gives your code sockets like that.

scenes.head: The smell: an if chain that keeps growing
scenes.say: This price function checks the customer kind with an if chain. It works, and prints seventy for a vip. But every new customer type means editing this function again, and risking the old ones. That is the smell. The function must change for every new rule.

scenes.head: The refactor: one class per rule
scenes.say: Now each rule is its own class. The base class defines the shared promise, apply. Student and Vip each keep one rule. Same output, seventy. A new rule is a new class. Nothing existing is edited. That is the open closed idea: open to extension, closed to modification.

scenes.head: SOLID: five habits, one line each
scenes.say: Single responsibility: a class has one reason to change. Open closed: extend by adding code, not editing. Liskov: a subclass must work anywhere its parent works. Interface segregation: small focused interfaces, not one giant one. Dependency inversion: depend on abstractions, like the socket, not on concrete details.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: Prefer composition, inherit for true is-a
No, wait for a second case first
scenes.say: Likely follow-ups. Inheritance or composition? Prefer composition, and inherit only for a true is a relationship. Liskov in one line: a subclass must work wherever its parent does. Is SOLID always right? No. Wait for a second case before abstracting. The four pillars: encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism. The mistake is reciting SOLID with no example.

lines: Object oriented design means code depends on small interfaces, not details.
SOLID: one job per class, extend don't edit, subclasses keep promises.
Example: replace an if chain with one class per rule.
scenes.say: Object oriented design means code depends on small interfaces, not details. SOLID is one job per class, extend instead of edit, and subclasses that keep their promises. For example, replace a growing if chain with one class per rule.
